places.name: Plaza Mayor
places.description: Enclosed 17th-century arcaded square with the equestrian statue of Philip III — the heart of Habsburg Madrid.

places.name: Mercado de San Miguel
places.description: Glass-and-iron market hall from 1916, now full of gastro stalls for tapas and jamón. Two steps from Plaza Mayor.

places.name: Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral
places.description: Western Europe's largest royal palace by floor area, with Almudena Cathedral opposite — seen from outside, from the esplanade.

places.name: Plaza de Oriente and Teatro Real
places.description: The opera house and the semicircle of Visigothic king statues facing the palace.

places.name: Plaza de España
places.description: Cervantes monument with Don Quixote and Sancho Panza, flanked by the 1950s skyscrapers Edificio España and Torre de Madrid.

places.name: Temple of Debod
places.description: A genuine 2nd-century BC Egyptian temple, gifted to Spain and rebuilt stone by stone. A good sunset spot.

places.name: Gran Vía and Callao
places.description: The 1910s showpiece boulevard: Edificio Carrión with the Schweppes neon sign, old cinemas and the Metrópolis building. Filmed in The Day of the Beast and in the empty-street dawn of Open Your Eyes.

places.name: Puerta del Sol
places.description: Kilometre zero of Spain's road network and the Bear and Strawberry Tree statue, the symbol of the city.

places.name: Círculo de Bellas Artes rooftop
places.description: Rooftop terrace (paid lift) with one of the best views over the centre. The rooftop panorama in Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown was shot from here.
films: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown

places.name: Plaza de Cibeles
places.description: The Cibeles fountain and Palacio de Cibeles, the city hall with a viewing terrace at the top.

places.name: Puerta de Alcalá
places.description: Neoclassical triumphal gate from 1778 at the entrance to the Retiro.

places.name: Retiro Park: Great Pond
places.description: The large boating lake with the Alfonso XII colonnade monument, the centre of Retiro Park.

places.name: Palacio de Cristal
places.description: Glass-and-iron pavilion from 1887 beside a pond in the Retiro, now an exhibition space of the Reina Sofía museum.

places.name: Fountain of the Fallen Angel
places.description: One of the few public monuments to Lucifer in the world, said to stand 666 m above sea level. The finale of The Day of the Beast takes place here.

places.name: Prado Museum
places.description: Seen from outside today: the façade and the Paseo del Prado boulevard, with the Velázquez statue at the entrance.

places.name: Reina Sofía Museum
places.description: Home of Picasso's Guernica. In Jarmusch's The Limits of Control the hitman walks in here; outside are Jean Nouvel's glass lifts.

places.name: Madrid Atocha Station
places.description: A tropical garden under the iron vaults of the old station hall. The day's walk ends here.

places.name: Cerralbo Museum
places.description: A marquis's mansion left as it was in 1922: paintings, weapons and crystal up to the ceiling. Near Plaza de España and Debod.

places.name: San Antonio de los Alemanes
places.description: A tiny oval church whose walls and dome are entirely covered in Baroque frescoes. Near Gran Vía and Callao.

places.name: House of the Seven Chimneys
places.description: 16th-century house where a woman's skeleton was found inside a wall — supposedly Philip II's lover, whose ghost is said to walk the roof. Near Cibeles.

places.name: Alfonso XII Monument viewpoint
places.description: You can climb into the colonnade above the Retiro pond for a view over the whole park and the centre.

places.name: Prince of Anglona Garden
places.description: A tiny walled 18th-century garden — step inside and the city disappears. Near the Royal Palace and La Latina.

places.name: Temporary Bauhaus-Archiv and Bauhaus Shop
places.description: The Bauhaus-Archiv's temporary home with the official Bauhaus shop — a quick design stop to start the day.

places.name: Bahnhof Zoologischer Garten
places.description: West Berlin's old main station, the setting of Christiane F.

places.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
places.description: The war-damaged church tower on Breitscheidplatz, a location in Wings of Desire.

places.name: LEGO Store Berlin
places.description: A quick stop to collect a stamp in the LEGO Passport.

places.name: Shell-Haus
places.description: Classic modernist office building — worth the detour for the façade alone.

places.name: Bendlerblock (German Resistance Memorial Center)
places.description: The courtyard where Stauffenberg and his fellow conspirators were shot after the 20 July 1944 plot.

places.name: Neue Nationalgalerie
places.description: Mies van der Rohe's glass-and-steel gallery; walk around the building from outside.

places.name: Berlin State Library (Potsdamer Straße)
places.description: The State Library on Potsdamer Straße, a location in Wings of Desire.

places.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
places.description: Walk through the field of concrete stelae. Marked as a mandatory stop.

places.name: Hansa Studios
places.description: Recording studio by the former Wall: Bowie's "Heroes", plus Iggy Pop, Eno, Nick Cave, Depeche Mode and U2.

places.name: Topography of Terror
places.description: Site of the former Gestapo and SS headquarters; walk through the grounds and along a surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall.

places.name: Victoria late-night shop (Späti)
places.description: The real Späti from the single-take film Victoria; its actual owner played himself.

places.name: Anhalter Bahnhof ruin
places.description: A single surreal fragment of façade is all that remains of the vast pre-war terminus. Emigrant and Kindertransport trains left from here — and, during the war, deportation trains.

places.name: Platz der Luftbrücke U-Bahn station
places.description: The station and underground passage from the famous Isabelle Adjani scene in Possession. Not a museum — recognise it and walk on.

places.name: Tempelhofer Feld
places.description: The former Tempelhof airport, one of the largest open spaces in the city. Step onto the field, take in the scale of the runways and carry on.

places.name: Schwerbelastungskörper (Germania test load)
places.description: 12,000 tonnes of concrete poured to test whether Berlin's soil could carry the giant triumphal arch planned for the Nazi capital 'Germania'. Grounds have limited opening hours.

places.name: Pallasbunker and Pallasseum
places.description: A 1943–45 bunker that could not be demolished, so the 1970s Pallasseum housing block was built right over it on stilts.

places.name: Former Stasi Headquarters (Normannenstraße)
places.description: The vast administrative complex of the GDR Ministry for State Security and a real location of The Lives of Others. The museum is optional — walking through the Campus für Demokratie is enough.

places.name: Frankfurter Tor
places.description: Monumental towers that open the grandest Stalinist stretch of Karl-Marx-Allee. The area is also linked to street scenes in The Lives of Others.

places.name: Café Sibylle
places.description: A short coffee stop right on Karl-Marx-Allee, with a small exhibition on the history of Stalinallee.

places.name: Strausberger Platz
places.description: One of the most ceremonial ensembles of socialist Berlin and a filming location of Good Bye, Lenin!

places.name: Kino International and Café Moskau
places.description: Two near-neighbours from a different 1960s East Berlin: instead of Stalinist pomp — glass, mosaics and light modernist volumes.

places.name: Karl-Marx-Allee 24 — the flying Lenin
places.description: Where Christiane steps out and sees the dismantled Lenin statue float past under a helicopter — one of the key images of Good Bye, Lenin!

places.name: Berolinastraße 21 — the Kerner family home
places.description: Exterior of the Kerner family's apartment block, around which much of the everyday world of Good Bye, Lenin! is built.

places.name: Haus des Lehrers
places.description: Look up at 'Unser Leben', a 125-metre socialist mosaic frieze that wraps the building and depicts ideal life in the GDR. On Alexanderplatz.

places.name: Hackesche Höfe and Scheunenviertel
places.description: Eight connected courtyards with Jugendstil façades in the old Spandauer Vorstadt / Scheunenviertel — easy to walk straight through.

places.name: Clärchens Ballhaus
places.description: Historic dance hall that stood in for a Paris café in Tarantino's Inglourious Basterds.

places.name: Berlin Wall Memorial (Bernauer Straße)
places.description: Not the East Side Gallery: here the logic of the border itself is preserved — the former death strip, wall segments and the street where in 1961 house façades literally became the border.

places.name: Hamburg Central Station
places.description: Start of the walk.

places.name: Rathausmarkt and Hamburg City Hall
places.description: The main city square and town hall — a quick pass without a separate stop.

places.name: Nikolaifleet
places.description: One of the most atmospheric old canals in the centre.

places.name: Deichstraße
places.description: Historic houses on the canal — much more interesting than an ordinary walk through the centre.

places.name: Chilehaus and Kontorhaus District
places.description: Expressionist brick architecture and the famous ship's-bow corner of the Chilehaus.

places.name: Speicherstadt
places.description: Red-brick warehouses, canals and bridges.

places.name: Magellan Terraces
places.description: HafenCity and views over the water; a good point to begin the walk along the Elbe.

places.name: Elbphilharmonie
places.description: The city's main modern symbol — seen from outside.

places.name: Traditionsschiffhafen
places.description: A small harbour full of old historic vessels — a less obvious stop.

places.name: St. Pauli Landungsbrücken
places.description: The classic view over the port and the Elbe. Planned food stop: a Fischbrötchen here (for example at Brücke 10) — try Matjes, Bismarck herring, smoked fish or North Sea shrimp.

places.name: Old Elbe Tunnel
places.description: Walk under the Elbe on foot — one of the most unusual free parts of the route.

places.name: St. Michael's Church (Michel)
places.description: Hamburg's main historic church; we walk past.

places.name: Zum Goldenen Handschuh
places.description: The real bar from The Golden Glove. The film is a bonus — the place is interesting in its own right.

places.name: Große Freiheit
places.description: The street of St. Pauli nightlife history and the early Beatles.

places.name: Beatles-Platz
places.description: A small square that serves as a Beatles memorial.

places.name: Feldstraße Bunker
places.description: A huge former military bunker with a modern extension on top.

places.name: Karolinenviertel
places.description: A lively alternative neighbourhood; walk through the side streets.

places.name: Schanzenviertel
places.description: Bars, graffiti and a completely different side of the city.

places.name: Dockland
places.description: An unusual building on the water; a strong architecture stop with a view of the port.

places.name: Große Elbstraße
places.description: Walk along the Elbe past fish restaurants and working-port atmosphere.

places.name: Hamburg Fish Market
places.description: Finish by the water. If the market is open, a good place for local fish.

places.name: Louvre Museum
places.description: The Louvre courtyard and galleries — the run through the museum in The Dreamers, the Winged Victory staircase in Funny Face and the pyramid of The Da Vinci Code.

places.name: Pont de Bir-Hakeim
places.description: Two-level steel bridge with the metro running on top, where Last Tango in Paris opens.

places.name: Saint-Étienne-du-Mont steps
places.description: The church steps on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève where the old car picks up Gil at midnight in Midnight in Paris.

places.name: Square Louis XVI
places.description: Quiet square around the Expiatory Chapel, a location in Bertolucci's The Conformist.

places.name: Moulin Rouge
places.description: The red windmill cabaret of Pigalle that gave its name to Baz Luhrmann's musical.

places.name: Café des Deux Moulins
places.description: The Montmartre café where Amélie works as a waitress.

places.name: Rue Foyatier stairs
places.description: The long staircase up to Sacré-Cœur from the stair fight in John Wick.

places.name: Pont Neuf
places.description: The oldest standing bridge in Paris, the setting of The Lovers on the Bridge (Les Amants du Pont-Neuf).

places.name: Shakespeare and Company café
places.description: The café of the Left Bank English bookshop where Before Sunset begins.

places.name: Place de la Concorde
places.description: The largest square in Paris, with the obelisk and fountains — the Paris fountain scene in The Devil Wears Prada.

places.name: Caveau de la Huchette
places.description: Historic jazz cellar in the Latin Quarter, a location in La La Land.

places.name: Aurouze pest-control shop
places.description: Old pest-control shop with stuffed rats hanging in the window — the shop window in Ratatouille.

places.name: Café de Flore
places.description: Classic Saint-Germain café, a regular location in Emily in Paris.

places.name: Tuileries metro station
places.description: The metro platform from the 'Tuileries' segment of Paris, je t'aime.

places.name: Passerelle Léopold-Sédar-Senghor
places.description: Footbridge between the Tuileries and the Musée d'Orsay, a location in The Intouchables.

places.name: L'Écoute sculpture
places.description: Henri de Miller's giant stone head resting on a hand, in front of Saint-Eustache — a location in La Haine.

places.name: Pont Alexandre III
places.description: The most ornate bridge in Paris, a key location in Luc Besson's Angel-A.

places.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery
places.description: The city's most famous cemetery, the setting of the 'Père-Lachaise' segment of Paris, je t'aime.

places.name: Palais-Royal
places.description: Palace gardens and arcades with the Buren columns, a location in Mission: Impossible.

places.name: 36 Quai des Orfèvres
places.description: The historic Paris police headquarters on Île de la Cité that gives Olivier Marchal's thriller its name.

places.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
places.description: The Gothic cathedral on Île de la Cité, home of The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe
places.description: The triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées, circled at speed in Taxi.

places.name: Residence Rose Garden
places.description: Residential building used as a location in François Ozon's In the House.

places.name: Temple de la Sibylle (Buttes-Chaumont)
places.description: Small round temple on a cliff top in the Parc des Buttes-Chaumont, with a view over north-east Paris.

places.name: Waffle breakfast stop
places.description: The booklet's first stop: 'Time for breakfast. Ready for your first waffle?' — with a score card for crunch, sweetness, filling and taste.

places.name: Zinneke Pis
places.description: Bronze of a dog cocking its leg — one of the three 'pissing' statues the booklet asks you to find.

places.name: Jeanneke Pis
places.description: The squatting-girl counterpart of Manneken Pis, tucked into a dead-end alley — the second of the three statues.

places.name: Manneken Pis
places.description: The city's famous little bronze boy — the third of the three statues.

places.name: Mont des Arts
places.description: 'Three views of one city' — the view from above: the terraced garden looking over the lower town.

places.name: Royal Galleries of Saint-Hubert
places.description: 'Three views of one city' — the view through glass: the 19th-century glass-roofed shopping arcade.

places.name: Grand-Place
places.description: 'Three views of one city' — the view in the dark: the guild-house square at night.

places.name: Breakfast stop
places.description: Booklet meal page ('one normal one for me, because I'm normal' — an In Bruges quote): breakfast.

places.name: Lunch stop
places.description: Booklet meal page: lunch.

places.name: Dinner stop
places.description: Booklet meal page: dinner.

places.name: 'Let it go' stop
places.description: Booklet clue in the spirit of In Bruges: 'Let go here of everything that troubled you.'

places.name: Belfry of Bruges
places.description: The medieval bell tower on the Markt. 'In the film not everyone climbs to the top — someone stays below.'

places.name: Basilica of the Holy Blood
places.description: Small basilica on the Burg that keeps the relic of the Holy Blood ('not a violet, and not basil' is the booklet's pun). The booklet points here twice.

places.name: Canal boat ride
places.description: 'So, what do you like? Riding around and looking at things?' — a canal boat ride from the landings near Rozenhoedkaai.

places.name: Groeningemuseum
places.description: Fine-art museum with Hieronymus Bosch's Last Judgment, the painting Ray and Ken study in In Bruges. 'Not Magritte — and there's nothing scary about that.'

places.name: 'Wait for the call' stop
places.description: In Bruges reference — Ken waiting for Harry's phone call.
